subject: Price hold + laddered prepay proposal
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@finxco.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@finxco.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Looking to lock pricing at renewal — multi‑year/prepay options

Hi Irene,

Hope youre well. Our renewal with Redwood is coming up in Q4. Weve been modeling for potential LLM cost increases and would like to explore options to lock effective unit pricing through a multi-year prepay. Two things are top of mind:

- Can we structure a laddered prepay (year 1 / year 2 / year 3) that locks an effective rate but allows us to ramp consumption without wasting credits?
- Is there a way to include a price floor (hold) in the early years and a surge-protection clause if our usage spikes above committed tiers?

Wed appreciate a concise proposal and any indicative pricing to share with finance. Looking to make a decision by the end of September.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Finance, FinX Analytics
elena@finxco.com

---
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@finxco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Looking to lock pricing at renewal — multi‑year/prepay options

Elena,

Thanks for the clear ask — happy to put a few concrete structures on the table. High level thoughts:

1) Laddered prepay (3-year example):
   - Year 1: 40% prepay at rate A (hold)
   - Year 2: 35% prepay at rate B (slightly higher than A)
   - Year 3: 25% prepay at rate C (market-linked)

   This preserves unused credits via an annual carry-forward that decays (12-month runway) so credits dont feel wasted if you ramp slowly.

2) Price hold + surge protection:
   - Price floor: we guarantee rate A for all prepaid consumption in Year 1 regardless of market increases.
   - Surge protection: above committed monthly throughput we offer an on-demand cap price (capped at X% above rate A) and an automated fallback to a compatible lower-cost model if demand exceeds dedicated capacity.

Im attaching a worksheet (FinX_Prepay_Ladder_v3.xlsx) with concrete numbers and a short terms summary (Redwood_Terms_Summary.pdf).

Would love to align with your target effective $/token so we can tailor the Year 1/2/3 splits. Are you available for a 30-minute call early next week?

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachments:
- FinX_Prepay_Ladder_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet: laddered prepay scenarios)
- Redwood_Terms_Summary.pdf (one‑page terms and surge wording)

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Looking to lock pricing at renewal — multi‑year/prepay options

Irene, quick internal notes after reviewing the worksheet:

- If FinX wants a stronger price floor in Year 1 (e.g., A - 5%), we should increase Year 1 commit from 40% -> 50% to keep margin intact.
- The carry-forward decay: suggest 12 months with a 25% annual write-off after year 1 (keeps accounting simple).
- Surge cap: recommend tying the cap to a pre-agreed model family (e.g., rwd-7B-quantized) with a 20% cap over rate A rather than an absolute dollar number — this is much easier operationally.

Also flagged for legal: Karthik, please review the suggested surge-protection language in the attached PDF and the carry-forward mechanic for any compliance concerns.

-Marcus
VP, Revenue — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

2) Legal wants to see specific surge-protection and carry-forward language before we share with procurement. If possible, please include a short example calculation for a 2x spike month.

Were available for a call Wednesday morning PST. Also looping in Rajiv (procurement) to start a high-level procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Elena

Ive reviewed the terms and made three small changes in the attached PDF:

- Clarified that the carry-forward is a credit pool with a 12-month decay and a max rollover of 50% of the next years prepay (prevents perpetual accumulation).
- Tightened the surge cap clause to exclude third-party infra pass-throughs (we wont cap cloud egress/network pass-throughs).
- Provided a sample calculation for a 2x spike month showing how prepaid buckets are consumed first and any excess billed at the capped on-demand rate.

Turning this into a short amendment for signature should be straightforward — happy to help draft the DocuSign.
